message: Cards as the whole interface, Archivo, 3D imagery everywhere Type - Silkscreen and the bitmap direction are gone. The replacement was chosen by reading the card artwork rather than by taste: the prints set "Instructional" in a neo-grotesque and "DESIGN" in an ultra-bold slightly-condensed cut of the same family, and Archivo covers that whole range in one variable face — 100..900 weight and 62..125 width. The site's type now sits inside the poster instead of next to it. - Display goes genuinely big, mobile first: page titles are 53px on a phone and 112px on a desktop, at weight 800 with -0.045em tracking. A grotesque this heavy is made to be set enormous; at 40px it is just a bold label. - Every page that hand-sized its own hero for the bitmap face is back on the shared ramp, so all headings are one voice at one scale. Home - No buttons. The artwork is the title, the card is the button, the position in the stack is the index — so the caption heading, the Enter button and the four index slots all left the page. What remains is the one line the artwork cannot say and an 01/04 counter. - Tapping the front card turns it over in 3D and navigates as it lands: a half turn on Y, arced toward the lens through the midpoint so it does not spin on the spot, with the route firing at 78% so the next page is already arriving while the card is still moving. - The stack is a canvas, so the only path for a keyboard or a screen reader is the nav that replaces the old slots. It sits off-screen until focused rather than hidden outright — tabbing lands on a real, visible link, and focusing one turns the tower to match. Imagery - New UiCard3D gives every image on the site the stage's behaviour: a plane in space with a moving specular sheen and a lit rim. A mouse tilts it directly; a touch device drives it from the element's position on screen instead, so a phone gets the effect from the one input it always has. - Applied to the index rows, the cursor plate, the about portrait and the case-study gallery. Motion - useScrollProgress writes an element's journey through the viewport onto itself as --p/--pc, so type animates by scroll in pure CSS. Sampled from rAF, not scroll events: iOS fires those in bursts and stops entirely during momentum, which stutters then freezes anything bound to them. - Page titles drift against the scroll and shed weight as they travel. Fixes found while checking - The .t-display rule still carried the bitmap face's weight 400 and 1.28 leading, so every display heading on the site was rendering light and loose. - Replacing tags with a component dropped their intrinsic width/height, and lazy images below the fold then had no height at all — the case-study gallery collapsed to 2px rows. Card3D now reserves the box from an aspect ratio, with a "fill" mode for slots whose parent already defines the height. Verified on a phone first: tap-to-flip navigates, background taps do not, the first Tab lands on a visible link, reduced motion navigates without the somersault, exposure passes on all four cards, and no route overflows or carries a sub-44px target.
